signals.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
signals.content: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; retrieval/RAG relevance; large language model relevance. Final score: 90. Freshness: source age 0.98d.
signals.brief_en: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization – A recent OSINT‑derived study shows that LLM‑guided evolutionary search can be accelerated by replacing text‑based reasoning with latent‑space agents. Hundreds of low‑cost agents per iteration exchange KV‑cache information, apply a novelty filter on hidden‑state distances, and let a summarizer agent perform natural crossover. On 21 benchmark mathematical and scientific‑computing problems, SwarmEvolve achieved the highest average scores, reaching peak performance in 3–8 minutes versus ~60 minutes for comparable state‑of‑the‑art frameworks. Using Qwen‑3 8B, it even refined solutions previously discovered by AlphaEvolve. The results suggest that latent‑space swarm communication offers a fast, cost‑effective route for program search in scientific domains, though further validation on larger problem sets is needed.
signals.brief_ar: SwarmEvolve: أسراب الوكلاء الكامنة للاكتشاف التطوري والتحسين – تُظهر دراسة مستندة إلى OSINT أن البحث التطوري الموجه بنماذج اللغة الكبيرة يمكن تسريعه عبر استبدال التفكير النصي بالتفكير في الفضاء الكامن. يعمل مئات الوكلاء منخفضي التكلفة في كل جولة على تبادل مخازن KV، وتطبيق مرشح الجدة بناءً على مسافات المتجهات المخفية، وتتيح وكيل الملخص إجراء تقاطع طبيعي للأفكار. على 21 مشكلة رياضية وحسابية علمية، حقق SwarmEvolve أعلى متوسط ​​للنتائج، ووصل إلى الأداء الأمثل خلال 3‑8 دقائق مقارنةً بـ ~60 دقيقة للأطر المماثلة. باستخدام Qwen‑3 8B، حسّن حلول AlphaEvolve السابقة. تشير النتائج إلى أن التواصل في الفضاء الكامن بين الأسراب يوفر نهجًا سريعًا ومنخفض التكلفة للبحث عن برامج علمية، مع ضرورة مزيد من التحقق على مجموعات مشاكل أوسع.

signals.title: @MarioNawfal: 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran-linked ships have been spotted making suspicious movements directly above critical underwater internet cables in the Gulf of Oman.
signals.content: 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran-linked ships have been spotted making suspicious movements directly above critical underwater internet cables in the Gulf of Oman. At least four vessels, including three U.S.-sanctioned tankers, have reportedly slowed down, circled cable routes and switched off their tracking systems at unusual moments. Maritime intelligence firm Windward says their movements are consistent with potentially mapping cable locations or placing explosives, although no sabotage has been confirmed. The activity follows explicit warnings from Iran's Revolutionary Guard that underwater internet cables, AI facilities and data centers could become targets if the U.S. and Israel launch another bombing campaign. The stakes are enormous. Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar depend entirely on cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz for international internet connectivity. Damaging them could disrupt banking transactions, communications, cloud computing and digital businesses across the Gulf. With Washington continuing to move military assets toward the region, Tehran appears to be signaling that another war could threaten far more than oil shipments. Source: Financial Times / Writer: Mhedi

signals.content: Jack — a local-first autonomous AI agent built on the COOLEMS framework: a just relay SERVER + smart CLIENT with file, browser, Python and vision tools, running on your own hardware via llama.cpp. Free for individuals; companies need a licence from Coolems KG.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: coolems/Jack

Jack is a locally‑hosted autonomous AI agent built on the COOLEMS framework. The architecture combines a lightweight relay server with a smart client that can access files, browse the web, execute Python code and perform vision tasks using llama.cpp on the user’s own hardware. The software is free for personal use; commercial deployments require a licence from Coolems KG.
